note:
ALA-LC Thai Romanization Table, 2011 version (earlier version: 1997), pp. 1-16; held source interscript-private-references/alalc/alalc-thai.pdf (sha256 d2156ef0927cb650e36c0cd96ead9f759eb8a38788d09a7274c32c521607a125; the duplicate alalc-thai.pdf.pdf is byte-identical). Extraction: the PDF text layer is real Unicode throughout (Word PDFMaker over Times New Roman / ArialUnicodeMS / CordiaNew; the only PUA span is U+F008, a missing-glyph box in the consonant table's ayn cell); every printed row was cross-checked against rendered page images (300 dpi pages, 600-1200 dpi cell crops).
Correction table (text layer -> print): the อำ cell and the Word Division คำ print the DECOMPOSED spelling (อ/ค + U+0E4D nikhahit + U+0E32); transcribed as the canonical single character ำ U+0E33 (the map's and the hand tests' encoding; compatibility-equivalent, identical rendering). The ayn prints as U+2018 in the table cell (followed by the PUA missing-glyph box) and in all 29 example occurrences; the gloss names "(ayn)" and the map uses the ayn U+02BB - map form kept, lookalike divergence recorded (the khm #328 / bod F12 class). Rule 4's value token: the text layer carries capital I (U+0049; advance 0.28 em at 11 pt, ArialUnicodeMS) with an italic-serif rendering in which capital I and lowercase l are glyph-indistinguishable; the print's own encoding says I, the map encodes Ia, the row passes - the conventional "la" reading is recorded for the maps-fix pipeline. The 900 dpi crop of the เอือย cell confirms the horn-u render (the horn draws as a small comma-mark at the u's upper right): the อวย row's ūai (U+016B U+0061 U+0069) is visually distinct from the เอือย row's ư̄ai (U+01B0 U+0304 U+0061 U+0069) exactly as the text layer encodes them.
Testing frame (the lao #326 convention): the vowel table prints its cells in the zero-consonant carrier form (อ + sign); the consonant table prints grouped letters with initial and final values. Each vowel sign is tested in its ก-carrier composition (the sign's printed value composed with ก; กา -> kā tests the า sign's ā), each consonant's initial value in the Cา frame (C + า = initial + ā) and its final value in the กาC coda frame (า + C = ā + final; the lao ກາC frame). Bare single letters are position-ambiguous under the map's final-value rules and are documented (finding 3), not row-tested. The iscrs runtime (interscript-rs 0.2.x; `after` = a following-text lookahead) classified every candidate row; every generated row's value is the printed value, verified byte-identical at runtime.
Findings (map-vs-source; transcribed rows EXCLUDED from the generated tests, never forced green; record for the maps-fix pipeline; page anchors to the 2011 print):
1. O-ANG OVER-APPLICATION (MAJOR, systematic; Note 3, p. 2). Note 3 silences อ "in four common words" preceding another consonant, but the map's unconditional อ+C -> initial rules fire on every อ+consonant sequence and eat the inherent-vowel อ before the CV grid composes it: น้อง -> nng (print nǭng), ท้อง -> thng (print thǭng), มองดู -> mngdū (print mǭngdū). The same interference makes two encoded rules unreachable: กอย -> kǭi never fires (printed ออย -> ǭi gives ky) and เกือย -> kư̄ai never fires (printed เอือย -> ư̄ai gives kēืy), because the อย/อว rules consume อ+C first. Words with อ word-finally (ข้อ khǭ, พ่อ phǭ) pass.
2. HO HIP HAS NO STANDALONE RULE (the lao #326 F1 class; row ห,ฮ, p. 2; Note 4). The printed initial value h has no bare rule: bare ห passes through (ห -> ห; หา -> หā). The ho-hip rewrite (ห+C -> Latin) also strands a following Thai อ the grid can no longer consume: หมอ -> mʻ (print mǭ), and ทรอ -> sʻ via ทร -> s (the consonant table's ทร cell) - the print composes หม+s+อ as mǭ/sǭ.
3. FINAL-VALUE RULES FIRE IN ONSET-CLUSTER POSITION (MAJOR, positional heuristic). `from C to FINAL after boundary` / `after any(<consonants>)` are following-text lookaheads at runtime, so a word-initial bare consonant followed by another consonant or by end-of-text takes its FINAL value: ดวง -> twng (print dūang), บท -> pt (print bot), คน -> kn (print khon), ต้น -> tn (print ton). A lone bare token likewise returns the final value (จ -> t, not čh; 31 of the 43 letters differ) - the initial column is row-tested only through the Cา frames (จา -> čhā passes). The 12 letters whose final equals their initial pass either way.
4. COMBO VOWEL ROWS UNENCODED (the generator's combo list, tools/gen-thai.py, was defined but never emitted): เอาะ -> ǫ (เกาะ -> kaoa), เออะ -> œ (เกอะ -> kēʻa), เออ/เอิ -> œ̄ (เกอ -> kēʻ, เกิ -> kēi), เอียะ -> ia (เกียะ -> kēīya), เอีย -> īa (เกีย -> kēīy), เอือะ -> ưa (เกือะ -> kēืʻa), เอือ -> ư̄a (เกือ -> kēืʻ; the เ lead digraphs consume เ+ก before the Cือ grid rule can fire - กือ -> kưa itself passes).
5. MACRON LOSSES (value divergences): อัว,ว -> ūa (U+016B; map กัว -> kua, macron dropped); standalone ว -> ūa (map -> w, the bare consonant); อื -> ư̄ (no Cื rule; กื -> kื, the sign leaks).
6. เอย -> œ̄i: unencoded (เกย -> kēy). The map's เCยย -> kœ̄i rule (tools/gen-thai.py's ("เ","ยย","œ̄i")) is (a) unreachable - อวย-class interference - and (b) mis-spelled (double ย; the printed form is เ + C + single ย).
7. อวย -> ūai: unencoded (กวย -> kwy).
8. MAI CHATTAWA CELLS: the printed เอ็ (e) and แอ็ (æ) forms have no เ+C+็ / แ+C+็ rules; U+0E47 leaks (เก็ -> kē็, แก็ -> kǣ็). เด็ก -> dē็k (print dek) fails the same way.
9. ZERO-CONSONANT CARRIER READINGS (the lao #326 F6 class). The vowel table's bare-อ readings are unencodable statelessly: bare อ -> ʻ (the consonant table's ayn row owns the bare-letter rule; the โอะ,อ -> o reading has no rule), ออ -> ʻʻ (print ǭ). Every carrier cell fails identically (อะ -> ʻa, อา -> ʻā, อิ -> ʻi, ...); the sign values are row-tested through the ก frames instead.
10. RULE 5 INHERENT VOWELS (documented design - the map description names bare consonants "the composition point for a vocalization model"): the print inserts dictionary inherent vowels the map cannot statelessly produce - นคร nakhǭn (runtime nkhǭn; the map's own hand test 3 encodes exactly this divergence against Note 2's printed value), สวรรค์ sawan (twǭnnkh์ - also the รร an-reading and the silent thanthakhat), กรรม kam (kǭnnm - the รร a-reading), คน khon (kn), ต้น ton (tn), บท bot (pt), ดวง dūang (twng), เครื่อง khrư̄ang (khērืng), เด็ก dek (dē็k), อดทน ʻotthon (dtn).
11. THO THAN THAKHAT (Note 1, p. 2): prints in BOTH the ด,ฎ,ฑ (d) and ถ,ฐ,ท,ฑ,ธ,ฒ (th) rows; "usually th, occasionally d" - the map encodes th only; the d reading has no rule.
12. REPEAT SYMBOL (rule 3, p. 3): instruction row - "the syllable is repeated in romanization" carries no printed value, so it is not transcribed; the map's placeholder literal "(repeat)" stands (ต่างๆ -> tāng(repeat), print tāng tāng; the ๆ semantics are caller-level). Rule 2's ฯ example พระเทพรัตนราชสุดาฯ -> Phrathēppharatrātsudā composes its tail correctly (the ellipsis appears) but the word stacks capitalization, inherent vowels and word division - caller-level.
13. WORD DIVISION (pp. 3-16, rules 1-43, ~150 example words): word division is caller-level segmentation (rule 9: "text is divided into words according to the guidelines provided in Word Division below") stacked on Rule 5 dictionary inherent vowels and title capitalization; the section's multisyllabic/prefix/compound/title examples are out of the single-token row model and are not transcribed as rows - flagged per the vai/bod convention. The row-testable representatives ARE included: Word Division 1's monosyllables (คำ kham, ไทย Thai, พูด phūt - the first two are the map's hand tests 1-2, retained there; ไทย is a from-duplicate and is not regenerated; the printed capital Thai is caller-level capitalization) and Word Division 2(c)'s 28 single-syllable prefix words (pp. 4-5), of which 19 pass (พ่อ แม่ ลูก พี่ ผู้ นัก ชาว ข้า ราย ลาย นาย นาง ข้อ แผน ขี้ ใจ ช่าง วัย บุญ) and 9 are the findings above (น้อง คน เด็ก ต้น บท เครื่อง ท้อง ดวง หมอ).
Bookkeeping: 176 printed rows transcribed and checked: 146 generated (42 consonant onset frames, 38 coda frames, 30 vowel ก-carrier rows, 4 ฤ/ฦ rows, 10 numerals, 2 symbol rows, 21 example rows - คำ kham is generated (a distinct from from hand test 1's กำ); ไทย and นคร duplicate hand tests 2-3 and are retained there) + 30 findings rows excluded from generation (17 vowel-form readings: กื เก็ แก็ เกาะ เกอะ เกอ เกิ เกียะ เกีย เกือะ เกือ กัว กอย เกย เกือย กวย ว; 12 example words: นคร สวรรค์ กรรม น้อง คน เด็ก ต้น บท เครื่อง ท้อง ดวง หมอ; ho hip หา) + the classes documented without transcription: the อ-carrier readings (finding 9), the bare-letter final-value class (finding 3), the repeat symbol and tho-than-thakhat's d reading (findings 11-12), and the Word Division section (finding 13). The rows array carries the 146 generated rows exactly. Regenerating via scripts/gen-row-tests.mjs from this artifact reproduces the embedded block byte-for-byte.
